sources.title: Maurice Hamington and Maggie FitzGerald, 'Feminist Care Ethics Confronts Mainstream Philosophy' (2022)
sources.notes: Open-access editorial in Philosophies 7(5), 91. CC BY 4.0. The committed text provides a contemporary account of care ethics, its relational ontology, Gilligan's challenge to individualist abstraction, and current theoretical debates.

sources.title: Carol Gilligan, In a Different Voice: Psychological Theory and Women's Development (1982)
sources.notes: Harvard University Press book; copyrighted, metadata only. Gilligan argues that dominant accounts of moral development overlook a relational moral voice organized around responsibility, connection, and the avoidance of hurt.

sources.title: Nel Noddings, Caring: A Relational Approach to Ethics and Moral Education (1984; 2nd edition 2013)
sources.notes: University of California Press book; copyrighted, metadata only. Noddings develops care as an ethic of receptive attention, motivational displacement, and response within concrete caring relations.

sources.title: Virginia Held, The Ethics of Care: Personal, Political, and Global (2006)
sources.notes: Oxford University Press book; copyrighted, metadata only. Held argues that care is a moral practice and value with personal, political, and global implications, challenging the treatment of care as merely private or secondary to justice.
